outcome: The complex quadratic Fatou conjecture (density of hyperbolicity for the family z^2+c) remains open; no proof, disproof, or partial case settled it in the window, and the adjacent MLC-at-Feigenbaum-points result is a related but distinct question, not a case of this bullet.
summary: The bullet as worded is the classical complex Fatou conjecture: that the quadratic family f_c(z)=z^2+c is hyperbolic (has an attracting cycle) for an open dense set of parameters c. This is equivalent to 'density of J-stability' / 'density of hyperbolicity' in the complex quadratic family, and it remains wide open as of September 2026; the article's own Wikipedia page (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatou_conjecture) states only the bare definition and gives no indication of resolution, and no subsequent search turned up a proof, disproof, or partial resolution of the stated question itself. The triage flagged Dudko-Lyubich's 'MLC at Feigenbaum points' (arXiv:2309.02107, v1 Sept 2023 — before the frozen revision date of 26 Jan 2024 — with v2 Dec 2023 and a v3 in Dec 2025 timed to journal acceptance at Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS) and Dudko's December 2025 ICM survey note (arXiv:2512.24171) as possibly relevant. I read both. MLC at Feigenbaum points proves local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set, and hence of the corresponding Julia sets, at specific Feigenbaum (infinitely renormalizable, period-doubling and complex-tripling) parameters — points that lie on the boundary of hyperbolic components and are themselves non-hyperbolic. The logical chain in the field is: MLC (full local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set everywhere) implies triviality of fibers, which implies density of hyperbolicity for the whole quadratic family (via the Orsay notes / Douady-Hubbard framework). But MLC-at-isolated-points is not a restriction of the density-of-hyperbolicity statement to a sub-case — it establishes a structural/topological fact at specific non-hyperbolic parameters, not that a positive-measure or open set of nearby parameters is hyperbolic. It does not remove any territory from the 'is the hyperbolic locus open and dense' question, since Feigenbaum points are (measure-zero) boundary points, not intervals of parameters whose hyperbolicity status the conjecture asks about. This makes it a related result under the problem sharing intellectual machinery (renormalization theory) with the target conjecture, not a case of it under §3.1. I found no AI system credited in either paper — both are traditional human-authored proofs in the classical style of Dudko-Lyubich's prior work, with no acknowledgement of computational/AI assistance in the sections I could access. Also checked Kozlovski-Shen-van Strien-style results and other 2024-2026 arXiv listings for 'density of hyperbolicity' + quadratic/complex; all hits were either pre-2024 foundational papers (Lyubich 1997, Graczyk-Swiatek 1997, Kozlovski-Shen-van Strien for higher real degree) or tangential (Cantor Julia sets density-of-hyperbolicity paper from Sept 2025, arXiv:2509.09914, which is again a different class of rational maps, not the quadratic family itself, and hence a related problem, not this one). No withdrawn claims, no counterexamples, no bound movements found on the complex quadratic Fatou conjecture itself.
competing_reading: A looser reading could treat MLC-at-Feigenbaum-points as 'progress toward the machinery needed for Fatou' and classify status as progress with ai_role none, since it does chip away at open pieces of the broader renormalization program that the full Fatou conjecture sits inside. But the bullet asks specifically whether hyperbolicity is open and dense across parameter space, an existence/density claim (§3.1's rule that such claims move only when answered, not when the territory around them is mapped in more detail) — and a local-connectivity fact at isolated non-hyperbolic points does not narrow where non-hyperbolic parameters could hide in the way a case-restriction would. I judge 'open' / 'no_change_found' to be the better reading, but flag this as a genuine judgment call the triage pass also flagged.
what_would_settle_it: A proof (or disproof) that MLC holds everywhere on the boundary of the Mandelbrot set (full MLC), which the field agrees would imply density of hyperbolicity for the whole quadratic family via triviality of fibers; or a direct proof/counterexample of density of hyperbolicity itself, e.g. exhibiting a non-hyperbolic parameter with an open neighborhood of non-hyperbolic parameters, or a topological argument bypassing MLC.
